html:
The Mahra Sultanate ruled the Mahra lands of far eastern Yemen and the island of Socotra in the Arabian Sea. The map shows it from 1530 to 1700. It was ruled by the Banu Afrar family from the 1400s, from Qishn on the coast and later from Socotra.

The Mahra people speak Mehri, one of the old South Arabian languages that are not Arabic. Their country is dry hills and coast between Hadramaut to the west and Dhofar in Oman to the east, a region long known for frankincense.

In 1507 Portugal seized Socotra, hoping to control the mouth of the Red Sea, but left it in 1511. The sultans also fought the neighbouring Kathiri sultans of Hadramaut. In the 1800s the sultanate signed treaties with Britain and became part of the Aden Protectorate. It was abolished in 1967, when South Yemen became independent.
